plotSections.title: Cosmic Hierarchy and Kar's Influence
bullets: The gods clarified that elder gods and the other major deities cannot directly interfere in mortal affairs. Kar is not technically a god or deity; he is instead an extremely powerful entity, described as being comparable to a deity in power and more akin to a demon or devil. Because Kar is not subject to the same restriction, he can directly interact with mortals.
Grixto is therefore believed to be a mortal agent or proxy through whom Kar can establish his will in the mortal world. This remains an inference rather than a fully confirmed explanation.

Kar has been fighting the gods for a long time and has reportedly lost many of those conflicts. He is associated with the Astral Sea/Abyssal Plane, which are explicitly the same thing within the context of Atlas, and the party has been warned against going there.

plotSections.title: Nevarr and the Books
bullets: Nevarr is believed to have somehow narrated or written himself into one of his own books and now exists within a demiplane associated with his writings.

The party does not know whether the story is true or how to reach Nevarr. Collecting his books was discussed as a possible optional side quest, and a Feylord may potentially know how to access the relevant demiplane.

plotSections.title: The Raven Queen's Ascension
bullets: The party heard two accounts of how the Raven Queen, Nira, rose to power: one from the Raven Queen herself and another from Vecna. The accounts broadly agree on the major events but differ in important details.

The Raven Queen said she was once a mortal elf who died in battle. After her death, Narul encountered her near the Everfalls and offered her a means to continue existing. She accepted, learned from Narul how to harbor souls, and eventually overthrew him.

The Raven Queen struck Narul down but did not kill him, apparently because gods cannot simply be killed in this manner. She instead left him in the condition in which the party later encountered him in Gilbrick, framing this as repayment for the role he played in saving her.
The Raven Queen identified herself as Nira the War Princess. The exact name Narul originally used for her was discussed but remains uncertain.
Vecna's version was more antagonistic toward the Raven Queen and claimed that she was assassinated rather than killed in battle. The differing accounts remain unresolved.

plotSections.title: Council and Current Party Status
bullets: The session resumes with the party gathered in the council created by the ringing of the keystone. Present major figures include Ben, Mahali, Narul, the Raven Queen, and Vecna, alongside Elrus, Araden, Kit Anger, Juten Prime, and Plymouth Gawater.
The party was confirmed to have reached level 19.

Gerk is characterized as prone to spreading entertaining rumors; he intends to tell people that Walker may be a god because Walker has a dragon, may live indefinitely, and has previously been directly associated with godlike claims.
